task.description: Translate the listed Sai files from Russian into English, following decisions/0080-english-instructions.md exactly (read it first, including the glossary in item 5). Rules: (1) the meaning must not change — same rules, numbers, names, order of sections; do not shorten, improve or add rules; (2) keep unchanged every file name, identifier, field name, AP-NNN, REQ-NNN, ISS-NNNN, decision number, command, role code and code block; (3) the front matter keys stay, but name: and description: are written in English (the name keeps the form "Sai <Role> (CODE)"); (4) text that the owner or a customer reads and tool error messages stay in the original Russian when quoted, followed by a short English gloss in parentheses; (5) plain, short English sentences, one term per concept (use the glossary); (6) no computer paths and no names of other projects in the text; (7) write the file in place with the Write tool, do not run prettier on .md outside tools/. Do not use git checkout/reset/stash/clean and do not commit. Do not stop the demo server on port 4782. Before close run: cd tools && npm run handoffs-check and npm run traces. In result list the files you translated and anything you were unsure about (issues). Files to translate: .claude/agents/: architecture-auditor, audit-compiler, audit-planner, audit-scout, audit-triage, ba-analyst, backend-dev, code-design-validator, code-designer, code-fixer, coverage-auditor, dependency-auditor, design-qa-validator, doc-auditor (14 files).

result.summary: Translated the 14 role files of step 01 from Russian into English in place, following decisions/0080 and its glossary. Same sections in the same order, same rules and numbers. Front matter keys unchanged; name: keeps the form "Sai <Role> (CODE)", description: is now English. All file names, ids (AP-, REQ-, ISS-, Q, R), decision numbers, commands, field names and role codes are unchanged. The Russian that remains is only quoted on purpose, with an English gloss: the defect file field names and section titles (audit-triage, coverage-auditor, doc-auditor), the example owner phrase in ba-analyst, and the questions label О1, О2 in code-designer. Other agents' files were not touched.

issues.text: Names of dimensions and statuses that other files quote were translated to English: dimensions "Architecture", "Test coverage", "Dependencies", "Documentation", "Requirements"; the report marks "not checked" (was не проверено), "not confirmed" (не подтверждено), "nothing to test" (тестировать нечего), "criterion → test" table. WF-05, WF-03, WF-02 and tools/README.md are translated by other agents: ORCH should check that they use the same English words, and that tests which compare these words (if any) are re-pointed.

Section titles of other files are referenced in English translation ("What a defect looks like" for WF-03, "General rules for all roles" for handoffs.md, "Parts and dimensions" for WF-05, "What of the hook input is stored", "Check" and "Pixel Office" for tools/README.md, section "result"). They must match the headings chosen by the translators of those files.

The defect file format (Серьёзность / Статус / Найдено / Пункт планки, and sections «Что не так», «Доказательство», «Как исправить», «Маршрут», «Закрыто») and the mistakes log fields («Что случилось», «Почему это плохо», «Как правильно», «Где найдено») are kept in Russian with an English gloss, because they are field names of files that stay as they are. In audit-triage I added one explanatory sentence saying so; if WF-03 is translated with English field names, these three files need the same change.
In code-designer the label for questions to ORCH is kept as О1, О2 (Cyrillic О) because it is an identifier used in existing design files.
The remaining Russian in ba-analyst is one example owner phrase (business text), kept verbatim with a gloss per rule 4.
